trial_name.text: Study C13006 (UC induction and maintenance; corresponds to label UC Trials I and II)

citations.quote: - Study C13006: Induction and maintenance; UC

Study C13006 was designed and conducted to assess the safety and efficacy of vedolizumab for the induction and maintenance of clinical response and remission in patients with moderately to severely active UC. This study was a phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. The induction and maintenance therapies were studied in two separate phases within Study C13006.
- Study C13006: Induction and maintenance; UC
This study was a phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with separate induction and maintenance phases

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of ENTYVIO were evaluated in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (UC Trials I and II) in adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC) defined as Mayo score of six to 12 with endoscopy subscore of two or three.

population.text: Adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis defined as Mayo score of six to 12 with endoscopy subscore of two or three

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of ENTYVIO were evaluated in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (UC Trials I and II) in adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC) defined as Mayo score of six to 12 with endoscopy subscore of two or three.

endpoint.text: Induction: clinical response at Week 6. Maintenance: clinical remission at Week 52.

citations.quote: In UC Trial I, a greater percentage of patients treated with ENTYVIO compared to patients treated with placebo achieved clinical response at Week 6 (defined in *Table 3*).

In UC Trial II, a greater percentage of patients in groups treated with ENTYVIO as compared to placebo achieved clinical remission at Week 52, and maintained clinical response (clinical response at both Weeks 6 and 52) (Table 4).

n.text: UC Trial I: 374 randomized; UC Trial II: 373 randomized

citations.quote: In UC Trial I, 374 patients were randomized in a double-blind fashion (3:2) to receive ENTYVIO 300 mg or placebo by intravenous infusion at Week 0 and Week 2.

In UC Trial II, 373 patients were randomized in a double-blind fashion (1:1:1) to one of the following regimens beginning at Week 6: ENTYVIO 300 mg every eight weeks, ENTYVIO 300 mg every four weeks or placebo every four weeks.

result.text: UC Trial I clinical response at Week 6: 47% ENTYVIO vs 26% placebo (p<0.001; difference 22%). UC Trial II clinical remission at Week 52: 42% (every 8 weeks) vs 16% placebo (p<0.001; difference 26%).

citations.quote: - Study C13007: Induction and maintenance; CD

Study C13007, very similar in design as the UC study (C13006), was conducted to assess the safety and efficacy of vedolizumab for the induction and maintenance of clinical response and remission in patients with moderately to severely active CD.

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of ENTYVIO were evaluated in three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials (CD Trials I, II, and III) in adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CD) (Crohn's Disease Activity Index [CDAI] score of 220 to 450).1

endpoint.text: Induction: clinical remission (CDAI <=150) at Week 6. Maintenance: clinical remission at Week 52.

citations.quote: In CD Trial I, a statistically significantly higher percentage of patients treated with ENTYVIO achieved clinical remission (defined as CDAI \le 150) as compared to placebo at Week 6 (Table 5).
In CD Trial III a greater percentage of patients in groups treated with ENTYVIO as compared to placebo were in clinical remission (defined as CDAI score \le 150) at Week 52.

n.text: CD Trial I (induction): 368 randomized; CD Trial III (maintenance): 461 randomized

citations.quote: In CD Trial I, 368 patients were randomized in a double-blind fashion (3:2) to receive ENTYVIO 300 mg or placebo by intravenous infusion at Week 0 and Week 2.

In CD Trial III, 461 patients were randomized in a double-blind fashion (1:1:1) to one of the following regimens beginning at Week 6: ENTYVIO 300 mg every eight weeks, ENTYVIO 300 mg every four weeks or placebo every four weeks.

result.text: CD Trial I clinical remission at Week 6: 15% ENTYVIO vs 7% placebo (p=0.04; difference 8%). CD Trial III clinical remission at Week 52: 39% (every 8 weeks) vs 22% placebo (p=0.001; difference 17%).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=3% and >=1% higher than placebo) included nasopharyngitis (13% vs 7%), headache (12% vs 11%), arthralgia (12% vs 10%), nausea (9% vs 8%) and pyrexia (9% vs 7%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 7% of ENTYVIO patients vs 4% placebo. Warnings include infusion/hypersensitivity reactions, infections, PML, and liver injury.
